atoms.b: The Taj Mahal was built around 400 years ago by an emperor in memory of his late wife. Around 20,000 workers helped build the famous ((++marble glass)) monument.
It is one of the Seven Wonders of the World and attracts around 7 ((++million billion)) tourists each year, making it one of the most visited landmarks in the world.

hint.label: Seven Wonders of the World
hint.text:
The Seven Wonders of the World are iconic global landmarks:

• Great Wall of China (China)
• Petra (Jordan)
• The Colosseum (Italy)
• Chichen Itza (Mexico)
• Machu Picchu (Peru)
• Taj Mahal (India)
• Christ the Redeemer (Brazil)
hint.sound: The Seven Wonders of the World are iconic global landmarks.

atoms.a: Sri Lanka, known as the Island of Gems, has gem deposits across 20–25% of its landmass.
Miners have dug more than 2 million deep gem pits across Sri Lanka over the past 50 years.
The gems are sent around the world, with the gem industry providing jobs for around 300,000 people across the country.
One of Sri Lanka’s most special gems is the pink-orange padparadscha sapphire, which is the country’s national gemstone.
atoms.sound: One of Sri Lanka’s most special gems is the pink orange pahdpahrahdschah sapphire, which is the country’s national gemstone.

hint.label: Seven Summits
hint.text:
The Seven Summits are the tallest mountains on each continent:

1. Mount Everest (Asia) - 8,849 m
2. Aconcagua (South America) - 6,961 m
3. Denali (North America) - 6,194 m
4. Mount Kilimanjaro (Africa) - 5,895 m
5. Mount Elbrus (Europe) - 5,642 m
6. Mount Vinson (Antarctica) - 4,892 m
7. Mount Kosciuszko (Australia) - 2,228 m
hint.sound: The Seven Summits are the tallest mountains on each continent.

atoms.b: Mount Everest is the ((++highest lowest)) of the Seven Summits, making it the tallest mountain on Earth. It stands at 8,849 metres tall on the border between Nepal and China.
Temperatures here can fall below -60 °C and ((++winds climbers)) can reach over 320 kilometres per hour, making it one of the harshest environments on Earth.

More than 7,000 people have successfully climbed Mount Everest since Sir Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay first reached the summit in ((++1953 2025)). Around 800 people still try to climb the mountain each year.

trainers.instruction: Read the text and answer the questions.

atoms.text: The Ganges is one of the most important rivers in South Asia, connecting India, Nepal and Bangladesh. Starting in the Himalayan Mountains, the river system provides water for millions of people.

For Hindus, the Ganges is the most sacred river in the world and is believed to have the power to cleanse sins. Every year, more than 100 million people visit the holy city of Varanasi to pray, bathe in the river and take part in religious ceremonies.
atoms.sound: For Hindus, the Ganges is the most sacred river in the world and is believed to have the power to cleanse sins. Every year, more than 100 million people visit the holy city of Vurahnahsi to pray, bathe in the river and take part in religious ceremonies.

atoms.text: As the Ganges reaches Bangladesh, it flows through the Sundarbans, the world’s largest mangrove forest. The Sundarbans is home to many endangered animals such as the Bengal tiger.

Which endangered animal can be found in the Sundarbans?
